nodes.label: Negative-Space Trace Symmetry Between Halves
nodes.rationale: Traces are knocked out of the coral fill as white negative space on the left, but drawn as positive coral/grey strokes on a transparent ground on the right. This inversion keeps a single visual weight across the mark while letting it sit on any background, and makes the logo legible at favicon size because the silhouette survives even when the interior detail collapses.

nodes.label: Solid Coral Organic Hemisphere with Neural Traces
nodes.norm_label: solid coral organic hemisphere with neural traces

nodes.label: Public Static Brand Asset (public/greydigi-logo.png)
nodes.rationale: Placed in the Next.js public/ directory, so it is served verbatim at the /greydigi-logo.png route and is referenced by path string rather than by import. Because the reference is a string literal, no AST edge exists between consuming components and this asset.

nodes.label: Human Intelligence Meets Digital Technology
nodes.rationale: The mark splits a brain down the midline: the left half is a solid coral organic cerebrum with white cutout traces ending in rounded terminal dots (dendrites/neurons), the right half is the same silhouette redrawn as printed-circuit routing with right-angle bends and ring-shaped vias fading from coral to grey. The rationale is that the two halves are the SAME shape drawn in two vocabularies, asserting that biological cognition and digital computation are one continuous system rather than opposed ones. The coral-to-grey fade encodes the company name itself (Grey + Digi) and lets the grey terminals recede so the coral side reads as the focal, warm, human element while the technology side reads as neutral infrastructure.

nodes.label: 0009_product_extensions.sql
nodes.rationale: Listed in CHECKLIST.en.md and GUIDE.en.md (which says run 0001 through 0009) but absent from the migration table in supabase/README.md — the README table appears stale.

nodes.label: 0002_core.sql
nodes.rationale: Holds workspace, people, RBAC, clients, notifications and audit log — the shared core every space depends on.

nodes.label: 0006_state_engine.sql — the authoritative state engine
nodes.rationale: One authoritative state/calculation engine (gate status, project health, progress, service health) plus triggers keeping cached columns in sync, so no screen recomputes its own numbers.

nodes.label: 0007_rls.sql — Row Level Security
nodes.rationale: Three enforcement tiers — internal workspace members, client-portal users, and the public boundary — so the client/public surface is constrained in the database, not just in the UI.

nodes.label: 0008_projections.sql — client/public projections
nodes.rationale: fn_publish_client_view, fn_public_share_view and fn_client_portal_project are the ONLY paths through which client/public code ever reads delivery data — a deliberate single choke point for the external boundary.

nodes.label: src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts
nodes.rationale: Currently hand-written to match the migrations exactly; regenerating with `npm run supabase:gen-types` against a real project replaces it with the authoritative version.

nodes.label: dev/ local stub auth and grants
nodes.norm_label: dev/ local stub auth and grants
nodes.rationale: local_stub_auth.sql and local_stub_grants.sql exist only to smoke-test migrations on bare Postgres that lacks Supabase's auth schema and anon/authenticated roles; they must NEVER be run against a real Supabase project, which already provides all of this.

nodes.label: seed_nk_live.sql — idempotent live client seed
nodes.rationale: Safe to run on production and safe to re-run: every insert uses a real unique constraint (on conflict do update) or an explicit find-or-create check, so re-running updates rows instead of duplicating them. Loads the aironauts flight plan as master template plus the Nutrition Kitchen 'Order to procurement' engagement from the Phase 1 kickoff deck.

nodes.label: seed.sql — demo portfolio
nodes.rationale: Seeds the same Nutrition Kitchen / Halcyon Freight / Beacon Dental / Ridgeline Outdoor data used by the design mockups, so every screen has something to show on first run.

nodes.label: Client Portal /portal/[project-ref]
nodes.rationale: Authenticated client view for people with kind='client' and a client_roles grant, where clients review progress and complete requested actions.

nodes.label: Client View Config → Publish
nodes.rationale: Nothing reaches the client portal or a public share link until an explicit Publish, so internal work-in-progress is never accidentally exposed; the 'last published' date is the confirmation signal.

nodes.label: Delivery Space
nodes.rationale: Client engagements: projects, flight plans, gates, tasks, baselines, change requests, client updates, and the client-facing layer.

nodes.label: Environment Variables (.env.local)
nodes.rationale: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL must match the app's real URL and be registered in Supabase Redirect URLs, otherwise email sign-in links break; the service_role key must stay private.

nodes.label: First Workspace Admin Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Manual SQL insert is a deliberate one-time bootstrap step because the app has no self-serve sign-up; everyone after the first admin is added from inside the app.

nodes.label: Google Sign-in (Supabase OAuth Provider)
nodes.rationale: Already wired in the app but off by default; a Google sign-in only creates a Supabase Auth account, so a matching `people` row is still required before workspace access.

nodes.label: Hypercare Space
nodes.rationale: Live client systems after go-live: services, incidents, requests, SLA, health, escalations.

nodes.label: Invite Flow (/people/invite)
nodes.rationale: Creates the Supabase Auth account and the `people` row in one step and shows a one-time temporary password; only a workspace admin may invite, checked both on the page and in the underlying action (defence in depth).

nodes.label: people Table (auth_user_id bridge)
nodes.rationale: A Supabase Auth user alone grants nothing; workspace identity, kind (internal/client) and workspace_role live in `people`, joined to auth via auth_user_id.

nodes.label: Product Space
nodes.rationale: Internal accelerators: products, roadmap, features, releases, engineering workload.

nodes.label: Public Share Page /s/[token]
nodes.rationale: A no-login, read-only project page lets clients and outside stakeholders see progress without provisioning accounts; it sits outside the internal app entirely.

nodes.label: Public Share Links (with Preview)
nodes.rationale: Preview shows exactly what an outside viewer sees, so the internal user can verify the public boundary before sending the link.

nodes.label: Workspace Core
nodes.rationale: Clients, people and roles, templates, notifications, settings, audit log and search are shared by all three spaces rather than duplicated per space.

nodes.label: greydigi workspace
nodes.rationale: One workspace with three spaces plus a public client-share layer, built from the greydigi Claude Design source and wired to Supabase.

nodes.label: Stack: Next.js 16 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, Supabase
nodes.norm_label: stack: next.js 16 app router, typescript, tailwind v4, supabase

nodes.label: Invite the First workspace_admin
nodes.rationale: No onboarding trigger is shipped because auto-creating the `people` row depends on each deployment's own invite flow.

nodes.label: Numbered Migrations (applied in order)
nodes.rationale: Strict numeric ordering encodes hard dependencies: enums before tables, tables before the state engine, state engine before RLS and projections.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md Include
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is a single-line pointer so the Next.js agent rules stay in one canonical file (AGENTS.md) rather than being duplicated per-tool.

nodes.label: Before Going to Production
nodes.rationale: Seed data is for demos/dev only, so the production decision defaults to not running supabase/seed.sql.

nodes.label: Setup Checklist (EN)
nodes.rationale: A tick-box condensation of GUIDE.en.md so an operator can verify each setup step without re-reading the prose.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: Most reported failures trace back to three causes: wrong env vars, migrations not run, or an auth user with no matching `people` row.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. The block is machine-written by `next dev`; deleting it from a diff only re-creates an uncommitted change, so committing it keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: Database-Computed State (single source of truth)
nodes.rationale: Every number on screen (gate status, project health, service health, release readiness) is computed by the database rather than typed on a page, so the same figure always agrees across every screen that shows it.

nodes.label: No Self-Serve Sign-up (provisioned access)
nodes.rationale: Access is provisioned deliberately rather than opened to sign-up, so no one can create their own way into a client workspace.

nodes.label: SQL-First Schema (no vendored Supabase CLI stack)
nodes.norm_label: sql-first schema (no vendored supabase cli stack)
nodes.rationale: The repo does not vendor the Supabase CLI local dev stack because `supabase start` needs Docker, which was unavailable in the authoring environment; migrations were smoke-tested against a plain local Postgres 16 instead.
